title: Sada-ASR: A Production Multidialectal Arabic Speech Recognition System
abstract: arXiv:2611.19512v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Callers to Arabic customer-service lines speak their own dialect, while speech recognizers are built and evaluated mainly on Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). A recognizer that mishears the dialect breaks the call before anything else can help. We present Sada-ASR, the speech recognizer of EchoNova's production Arabic voice agent. On a 120-hour test set of MSA and eight dialects, it has the lowest word and character error rates of twelve systems, against eleven from Microsoft, ElevenLabs, Google, OpenAI, Speechmatics, IFM, Cohere, NVIDIA and Audar: 11.69% word error rate against 13.51% for the strongest, Microsoft's MAI-Transcribe-2 (a lead of 0.74 points on clips unaffected by that system's fixed number and script conventions), and 15.52% against 16.96% averaged over varieties. Its largest margins are on Omani (4.30 points), Egyptian (3.78) and Saudi (2.19) speech; it is level on Syrian and loses on Lebanese (24.96% against 23.05%), mostly

translated_title: Sada-ASR：一个生产级多方言阿拉伯语语音识别系统
translated_abstract: 摘要：拨打阿拉伯语客服热线的来电者使用的是各自的方言，而语音识别系统却主要基于现代标准阿拉伯语（MSA）构建和评估。一个听不懂方言的识别器会在其他任何补救措施生效之前就使通话中断。我们提出 Sada-ASR，这是 EchoNova 生产级阿拉伯语语音助手中的语音识别系统。在一个包含 MSA 和八种方言的 120 小时测试集上，它在十二个系统中取得了最低的词错误率和字符错误率，对比的十一个系统来自 Microsoft、ElevenLabs、Google、OpenAI、Speechmatics、IFM、Cohere、NVIDIA 和 Audar：其词错误率为 11.69%，而最强对手 Microsoft 的 MAI-Transcribe-2 为 13.51%（在该系统固定的数字与文字书写规范不受影响的语音片段上领先 0.74 个百分点），在各方言变体上平均词错误率为 15.52%，对比 16.96%。其最大优势体现在阿曼方言（领先 4.30 个百分点）、埃及方言（3.78）和沙特方言（2.19）上；在叙利亚方言上持平，在黎巴嫩方言上略逊（24.96% 对比 23.05%），大多……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: Sada-ASR 是一个部署于真实客服场景的生产级阿拉伯语多方言语音识别系统，在涵盖 MSA 和八种方言的 120 小时测试集上以 11.69% 的词错误率超越 Microsoft、Google、OpenAI 等十一家竞品，取得全场最低错误率，尤其在阿曼、埃及和沙特方言上优势最大。
en_tdlr: Sada-ASR is a production-grade multidialectal Arabic speech recognition system deployed in real customer-service calls, achieving the lowest word error rate (11.69%) among twelve systems on a 120-hour benchmark covering MSA and eight Arabic dialects, outperforming competitors from Microsoft, Google, OpenAI, and others, with its largest margins on Omani, Egyptian, and Saudi dialects.
